comment: Stable W11 scenario inventory and negative attack matrix for the dedicated transfer browser release run. Scenario ids and attack ids are the release evidence contract: results are written as scenario-<id>.json and attacks.json entries keyed by these ids, and no required entry may be omitted from a bundle.

scenarios.title: new learner-owned checklist, unchanged legacy data, one structured draft for the teacher
teacher review, edit, reconfirm, and send delivers one four-option assessment while the room stays in tutoring mode
correct labels resolve exactly once, survive reload, and are followed by tutoring feedback rather than a second assessment
wrong answer records needs-review, offers repair, waits for new learner evidence, and uses a different context before a later pass
Guard active defers protected progression and applies the deferred event at most once on recovery
dirty or stale draft, reconnect catch-up, commit retry, second teacher tab, and duplicate learner answer create no phantom, stale, or duplicate effect
learner network, realtime, export, storage, and error surfaces carry no private material
forged identity, cross-learner, cross-room, stale-question, direct-write, and legacy-RPC operations are rejected with protected state unchanged
legacy checklist values stay legacy and are never presented as transfer-verified
release verdict stays not approved while any required gate or lane is not pass, and activation eligibility is recorded separately
rollback disables new generation and delivery without dropping tables, deleting evidence, or erasing history

attacks.expected_boundary: server rejects the forged principal and protected state is unchanged
a learner principal cannot read or mutate another learner's assessment
a principal outside the room is refused by room-scoped authorization
a stale question id is rejected rather than graded against a newer key
a direct table write cannot create or alter protected assessment state
a legacy RPC cannot submit or mutate a transfer assessment
